guardrails: No diagnosis or labels about the ex.
mechanic: One-liner with a clear claim that reframes blame.
insight: When a relationship ends badly, people assume they were the problem. The ex's behaviour is usually the issue.
hook: "It happened because something was wrong with that person, not with you."
reach: Women forward it to the friend who is still blaming herself after a breakup.
quiz_because: "Why do I always end up thinking the problem is me?"

name: Modo supervivencia recognition
guardrails: No clinical labels such as "trauma response" applied to a specific person.
mechanic: Single-sentence reassurance that names a behaviour pattern.
insight: Acting in ways you are not proud of, during a hard relationship, says more about the situation than about who you are.
hook: "How you acted in survival mode does not define who you really are."
reach: People save it for the moment they feel ashamed of how they reacted.
quiz_because: "Why did I become someone I don't recognise?"

name: Permission to leave
guardrails: Permission framing only; no fear or guilt.
mechanic: Short list of permissions, each starting with "You can".
insight: Many people stay in relationships because they think leaving is not allowed. It is always their choice.
hook: "You can leave. You can stand up from that table. You can start again."
reach: It reads like a hug and gets saved for a bad week.
quiz_because: "Why do I need permission to walk away?"

name: The "no" without compensation
guardrails: No labels about the friend, and no promise of cure.
mechanic: First-person micro-scene plus one expert verdict line.
insight: After saying no, she immediately offers a fix to avoid upsetting the other person.
hook: "I said no to a friend and, five minutes later, I was already offering her a solution."
reach: People forward it with "this is literally me".
quiz_because: "Why do I always make it up to people after saying no?"

posts:
1. > Decir que no y quedarte tranquila es una habilidad, no un rasgo de carácter.

name: Charm that comes too fast
guardrails: No labels or diagnoses about specific people.
mechanic: Contrast pair ("They teach us X, nobody prepares us for Y")
insight: Someone who is very charming and intense from week one is going fast, not deep. Watch what they do when you slow down.
hook: "We're taught to spot someone who treats us badly. Nobody prepares us for someone who treats us too well, too soon."
reach: "Mándaselo a tu amiga que acaba de conocer a alguien 'perfecto'."
quiz_because: "Why do I get hooked on people who move very fast?"

1. > Nos enseñan a detectar a quien nos trata mal. Pero nadie nos prepara para alguien que nos trata de maravilla... demasiado pronto.
   > Si en dos semanas ya te dice que eres «diferente a todas» y quiere verte cada día, no significa que seas especial para él. Significa que va deprisa.
   > Fíjate en lo que hace cuando le dices «vamos más despacio».

If within two weeks he says you're "different from all the others" and wants to see you every day, it doesn't mean you're special to him. It means he's going fast. Notice what he does when you say "let's go slower".*

   *EN: They say real love arrives with force from day one. I've seen the opposite many times: what arrives very strong and very fast tends to ask for the same in return, just as fast. If you feel overwhelmed and call it "chemistry", pause. You can go slower. Someone who cares for you well can too.*

name: Missing him isn't a reason to go back

mechanic: Pointed question to a specific group, followed by her own answer
insight: Many women go back to an ex because they miss how it felt in the good months, not because he changed.
hook: "Question for those who went back to an ex: did something change, or do you miss how it felt at the start?"
reach: "Mándaselo a la amiga que vuelve a hablar con su ex."
quiz_because: "Why do I keep thinking about someone who hurt me?"
